'''Pernilla Wittung-Stafshede''' (maiden name Wittung) is a Swedish [[biophysical chemist]], born in 1968, who is a professor of [[Chemistry]] at [[Rice University]] in [[Houston, Texas, USA]]. In 2019 she was named by [[International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry]] as a Distinguished Woman in Chemistry.

==Education==
She received her [[Master of Science]] Degree in [[Engineering]] from Chalmers University of Technology and a doctorate at the same institution in 1996 in biophysical chemistry under [[Bengt Nordén]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chalmers.se/chem/EN/divisions/physical-chemistry/nordenlab/former-members |title=Chalmers University of Technology &#124; Chalmers |website=www.chalmers.se |access-date=14 July 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121012034553/http://www.chalmers.se/chem/EN/divisions/physical-chemistry/nordenlab/former-members|archive-date=12 October 2012}}</ref> with a [[thesis]] entitled ''Intelligent nucleic acid interactions with peptide nucleic acids and in recombination proteins''.<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://publications.lib.chalmers.se/publication/1105-intelligent-nucleic-acid-interactions-with-peptide-nucleic-acid-pna-and-recombination-enzyme-reca |title=Intelligent Nucleic Acid Interactions with Peptide Nucleic Acid (PNA) and Recombination Enzyme RecA |website=publications.lib.chalmers.se |year= 1996|access-date=7 March 2017|last1= Wittung|first1= Pernilla}}</ref>

==Employment==
After her [[Ph.D.]], she worked for twelve years in the [[United States]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]], Beckman Institute in Pasadena, California (1997–98), [[Tulane University]] in New Orleans, Louisiana(1999-2003) and [[Rice University]] in Houston, Texas (2004-2008). In 2008, she returned to Sweden to a professor position at [[Umeå University]]. From 2015 to 2025 she was a professor at Chalmers University of Technology and was the head of the Chemical Biology division for the first 3 years.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date= |title=Pernilla Wittung-Stafshede new Head of Division of Chemical Biology |url=http://www.chalmers.se/en/departments/bio/news/Pages/Pernilla-Wittung-Stafshede.aspx |access-date=2017-07-17 |website=www.chalmers.se |language=en-us|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150629040638/http://www.chalmers.se/en/departments/bio/news/Pages/Pernilla-Wittung-Stafshede.aspx|archive-date=29 June 2015}}</ref>

In July, 2025, she moved to Rice University in Houston, Texas, to become the Charles W. Duncan, Jr.-Welch Professor of Chemistry. Concurrently she received an Established Investigator Award as a CPRIT Scholar.<ref>{{Cite web|title=State cancer agency awards $68 million in research grants to Texas institutions |publisher=Cancer Prevention and Research Institute of Texas|date=19 February 2025|url=https://www.cprit.texas.gov/news-events/articles/state-cancer-agency-awards-68-million-in-research-grants-to-texas-institutions/|language=en-us|access-date=2025-10-24}}</ref>

She leads a research group that focuses on the [[biophysical]] properties of [[proteins]]; both metal-transporting proteins and proteins that fold incorrectly and clump together. The research is basic science, but has links to diseases such as [[Alzheimer's]], [[Parkinson's]] and [[cancer]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pernilla Wittung-Stafshede|url=https://profiles.rice.edu/faculty/pernilla-wittung-stafshede|website=www.rice.edu|language=en-us|access-date=2025-10-24}}</ref>

In 2010, Pernilla Wittung-Stafshede was one of ten researchers in Sweden, appointed as a Wallenberg Scholar, receiving a grant awarded by the [[Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation]] that she has renewed several times (most recently in 2024).<ref>{{cite web | title=Wallenberg Scholars 2024 | website=Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation | url=https://kaw.wallenberg.org/en/wallenberg-scholars-2024 | access-date=2024-07-04}}</ref> In 2017 she was elected a member of the council of [[Biophysical Society]] (BPS). It was the second time ever for a Swedish scientist; the first one was Arne Engström 1960–1963.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.biophysics.org/AboutUs/Leadership/PastCouncil/tabid/2239/Default.aspx|title=Past Council|website=www.biophysics.org|language=en-US|access-date=2017-08-15}}</ref>

In 2020, she became a member of the Nobel Prize in Chemistry Committee,<ref>{{cite web |last=Royen |first=Ulrika |date=2018-08-14 |title=The Nobel Committee for Chemistry |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/organization/the-nobel-committee-for-chemistry/ |access-date=2024-07-04 |website=NobelPrize.org}}</ref> and since 2021 she is a council member for The Lindau Nobel Laureate Meetings.[https://www.lindau-nobel.org/member/pernilla-wittung-stafshede/] In 2019 she started Genie at [https://www.chalmers.se/en/about-chalmers/organisation-and-governance/equality/genie-gender-initiative-for-excellence/ Chalmers], a 300 MSEK gender equality initiative funded by the Chalmers Foundation and led it for four years.<ref>{{cite web | last=Karlsson | first=Robert | title="Many people at Chalmers want to engage in gender equality" | website=Chalmers tekniska högskola | date=2020-03-09 | url=https://www.chalmers.se/en/current/news/many-people-at-chalmers-want-to-engage-in-gender-equality/ | access-date=2024-07-04}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Pernilla Wittung-Stafshede has received a number of awards and prizes. These include:

* National Fresenius Award in 2003, awarded by the [[American Chemical Society]] [[Phi Lambda Upsilon]] to young eminent chemistry researchers.<ref>{{cite web|title=National Fresenius Award|url=https://chemgroups.northwestern.edu/geiger/PLU/National%20Fresenius%20Award.html|website=chemgroups.northwestern.edu|accessdate=7 March 2017}}</ref>
* [[Göran Gustafsson Prize]] in Chemistry in 2009, awarded by the Göran Gustafsson Foundation and the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]].
* [[Wallmark Prize]] in 2009, awarded by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.
* STIAS fellow in 2013, awarded by the [[Stellenbosch Institute for Advanced Studies]], South Africa.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fellows|url=http://stias.ac.za/fellows-of-stias/fellows-2013/|website=Stellenbosch Institute for Advanced Studies|accessdate=7 March 2017}}</ref>
* Svante Arrhenius plaque in 2016, awarded by the [[Swedish Chemical Society]] in collaboration with the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{cite web|title=List of recipients|url=https://kemisamfundet.se/utmarkelser/lista-mottagare/|website=Swedish Chemical Society|accessdate=7 March 2017}}</ref>
* Elected member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]], 2016.
* Elected member of the Royal Society of Arts and Sciences in Gothenburg, 2016.
* 2019 [[International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry]] Distinguished Woman in Chemistry<ref>{{Cite web |title=IUPAC Distinguished Women in Chemistry or Chemical Engineering |url=https://iupac.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/Recipients-IUPAC-Distinguished-Women-in-Chemistry-or-Chemical-Engineering_20210208.pdf}}</ref>
* Elected as a member, [[Academia Europaea]], 2017 <ref>{{cite web | last1=Hasani | first1=Ilire | last2=Hoffmann | first2=Robert | title=Academy of Europe: Wittung Stafshede Pernilla | website=Academy of Europe | url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Wittung_Stafshede_Pernilla | access-date=2024-07-04}}</ref>
* Gustav Dalén Medal, 2019<ref>{{cite web | title=Gustaf Dalén | website=Chalmersska Ingenjörsföreningen | url=https://avancez.se/en/about-us/gustaf-dalen | language=sv | access-date=2024-07-04}}</ref>
* Elected member Royal Swedish Academy Engineering Sciences, 2020<ref>{{cite web | title=Ledamot | website=IVA | date=2023-05-03 | url=https://production.iva.se/ivas-ledamoter/fbf7352a-9bfb-e711-80e9-00155d016a87/pernilla-wittung-stafshede/ | language=sv | access-date=2024-07-04}}</ref>
* Selected as Biophysical Society Fellow, 2022<ref>{{cite web | title=Biophysical Society Award to Chalmers Professor | website=Chalmers tekniska högskola | date=2021-11-09 | url=https://www.chalmers.se/en/current/news/life-biophysical-society-award-to-chalmers-professor/ | access-date=2024-07-04}}</ref>
* Selected as Honorary Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry (HonFRSC), 2024<ref>{{cite web | last=Lindh | first=Susanne Nilsson | title=Chalmers Professor new Honorary Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry | website=Chalmers tekniska högskola | date=2024-04-23 | url=https://www.chalmers.se/en/current/news/life-chalmers-professor-appointed-as-honorary-fellow-of-the-royal-society-of-chemistry/ | access-date=2024-07-04}}</ref>
* Elected as Fellow of the European Academy of Sciences, 2024
* Elected as Foreign Member of the Finnish Society of Sciences and Letters, 2024<ref>{{cite web | title=New members | date=2024-12-17 | url=https://scientiarum.fi/en/new-members/ | access-date=2025-10-25}}</ref>

== Bibliography ==
Pernilla has published several hundred scientific peer-reviewed articles since her first in 1994 and numerous popular articles.
Full list on her ORCID<ref name="w671">{{cite web | title=ORCID | website=ORCID | date=2024-07-08 | url=https://orcid.org/0000-0003-1058-1964 | access-date=2024-07-18}}</ref> or Scopus<ref name="e360">{{cite web | title=Wittung-Stafshede, Pernilla | website=Scopus | url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=7005808951 | access-date=2024-07-18}}</ref> sites.

== Personal life ==
Wittung-Stafshede has two daughters, Selma and Hilda Stafshede. Pernilla has two sisters, Paulina and Petronella.
